## FAQ

1. Rutile vs. Anatase --what's the difference?
:   Rutile offers better opacity, brightness, and weather resistance -- ideal for outdoor use. Anatase is more reactive, used for indoor or photocatalytic applications.

2. What specs matter most?
:   TiO2 content (93-96%), particle size (0.2-0.3um), brightness (95min), oil absorption (16-18), and surface treatment type.

3. Sulfate vs. Chloride process -- which is better?
:   Chloride process yields higher purity and better color consistency, with lower environmental impact - preferred for premium grades. Sulfate process is more common in China and cost -effective for general use.

4. How to choose the right grade?
:   Coatings --- rutile + surface treatment; Plastics --- good dispersibility; Inks --- fine particle size; Cosmetics/Food --- FDA-compliant grades.

5. What certifications should a supplier have?
:   ISO 9001, ISO 14001, REACH (for EU), FDA (for food/cosmetic grades), and third-party lab test reports.

6. Is TiO2 safe?
:   Low toxicity for skin contact and ingestion. Inhalation of dust is a concern -- use respiratory protection when handling powder.

7. Why is it expensive?
:   High refractive index (2.73), energy-intensive production, and rising raw material & compliance costs.

8. How to store?
:   Cool, dry, sealed containers. Protect from moisture to prevent caking.

9. Free samples?
:   Yes -- most suppliers offer 0.5--1kg free samples to qualified buyers. Always test in your formulation first.

**One of the most important components of paint is [Titanium Dioxide](/titanium-dioxide/), a opaque, opaque substance that gives the paint depth gloss and is used in the production of paint.**

**It is also widely used in the plastic industry, not only as a matte white pigment but also because of its UV resistance. In fact, titanium dioxide reduces the damage caused by ultraviolet light by scattering light due to its high refractive index. The use of titanium dioxide in plastics improves the appearance quality as well as the strength and mechanical properties of plastics. Titanium dioxide is used in the production of plastics, masterbatch, PVC, ABS, etc.**

BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment has outstanding dispersion performance, dispersing quickly and easily. It also has excellent opacity and gloss, and delivers a brilliant whiteness with a clean blue tone. With its carefully selected inorganic surface coating, BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment provides a high level of weatherability, making it flexible across both interior and exterior applications.

## Titanium Dioxide

Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) is a brilliant white inorganic pigment valued for its exceptional opacity, high refractive index, and stability . It is considered the world's most important white pigment, serving as a critical component in a vast array of products by providing outstanding whiteness, brightness, and hiding power

* Synonyms:

  Titania; Titanium(IV) oxide; TiO₂
* Formula:

  TiO₂
* CAS NO.:

  13463-67-7
* Package:

  25KG BAG
* Certificate:

  Reach, ISO9001

Our Achievement

**Global Reach:**Our  Titanium Dioxide has been successfully exported and applied in key markets across the globe, including but not limited to UAE, Thailand, Vietnam, Egypt, Brazil  etc.  Our product has consistent quality and ability to meet diverse international standards.

**Equivalent Alternatives:**We supply different brands of Titanium Dioxide, including Lomon billions, Taihai, panzhihua etc, and both rutile and anatase like R996, R5566, R218 etc, helping customers reduce costs with comparable (or even superior) results in performance.

Key Applications

* •Paints, Coatings, and Inks
* •Plastics and Rubber
* •Paper and Printing
* •Cosmetics and Personal Care

The main detailed uses of the product

* ![Paints, Coatings, and Inks](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

  Paints, Coatings, and Inks

  TiO₂ is a fundamental ingredient in architectural and industrial paints, providing excellent covering power (opacity), durability, and gloss . Its resistance to UV light makes it essential for exterior coatings that require long-term weather ability .
* ![Plastics and Rubber](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

  Plastics and Rubber

  In the plastics industry, TiO₂ is used to impart whiteness, opacity, and enhanced mechanical properties to products ranging from packaging to automotive parts . It improves heat resistance and weatherability in plastics and rubber applications .
* ![Paper and Printing](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

  Paper and Printing

  Titanium dioxide is used as a whitening and opacifying agent in high-quality paper grades and in printing inks, contributing to brightness, opacity, and print clarity .

# European Coatings Show: Product Spotlight

* Topic: [CoatingsTech Update](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/coatingstech-updates/), [Conferences](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/conferences/), [New Products](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/new-products/)

[![Open paint cans](https://www.paint.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/OCT15_paint-cans.jpg)](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/articles/european-coatings-show-product-spotlight/)

Share via:

* [Facebook](#)
* [Twitter](#)
* [LinkedIn](#)
* [Print](#)

*Editor’s note: This column is a roundup of product releases to be highlighted at the [2023 European Coatings Show](https://www.european-coatings-show.com/) (ECS) in Nuremberg, Germany. To submit a product release for consideration, email [aelliot@paint.org](mailto:aelliot@paint.org). Please note that all submissions are subject to editorial approval and publication is not guaranteed.*

**Penn Color Dispersions**

Penn Color, supplier of colors, additives, and compounds headquartered in Hatfield, PA, will be at the upcoming ECS to present their range of dispersions, which is composed of those that are water-based, solventborne, or energy-curable.

According to the company, their water-based dispersions have low to no VOCs and high pigment loading properties and are APEO- and binder-free. The solvent-based dispersions are broadly compatible with acrylic resin systems and have high pigment-loading and optimal rheological properties. The energy-curable dispersions are for 100% solids and multiple oligomers, require low curing energy, and are broadly compatible with various systems.

Learn more about [Penn Color](https://www.penncolor.com/)’s dispersions range at Stand 2-615 in Hall 2.

**Clariant Halogen-Free Flame Retardants**

Clariant plans to showcase three product lines focused on sustainability at ECS: Ceridust® additives, EcoTain® (which includes Exolit® AP 435 and Exolit AP 418, and VITA, which includes polyglycols (PEGs) and ethylene oxide derivatives.

Clariant’s Ceridust® additives are made to enable scratch-resistant protection for packaging barrier coatings with a good slip-effect and rub-resistant printing inks. The company says these additives are free of PTFEs and include polyethylene waxes and a biobased wax.

Two products that Clariant plans to feature are from its EcoTain® sustainability line. Exolit® AP 435 is intended to prolong the shelf life of finished products during storage and transportation, and Exolit AP 418 is designed for efficiency, thus reducing the industry’s material use. The latter product, according to Clariant, can achieve up to 10% longer fire-resistant time for a film applied at up to 25% less thickness than what is typical.

The VITA range includes polyglycols (PEGs) and ethylene oxide derivatives for use as surfactants and intermediates in paint and coatings production. The company states that VITA products are 100% based on plant-based carbon via bioethanol. These new ingredients are chemically equivalent to their fossil-based analogs and therefore offer the same performance and efficiency to formulators and brand owners, according to Clariant.

[Clariant](http://www.clariant.com) will be at Booth 322 in Hall 3A.

**Heubach Coil, Green, and UV Pigments**

The Heubach Group, a German-based manufacturer of organic and inorganic pigments and preparations, will unveil several new pigments at ECS: Heucosil™ CSA and CSM, Heucodur® Green 630, and Hostatint™ UV 100.

Heucosil™ CSA and CSM are zinc-free anti-corrosive pigments that the company says meet the performance requirements for coil- and thin-film applications. These products are designed for corrosion protection performance and low oil absorption.

Heucodur® Green 630 is a new non-labeled spinel green pigment based on a chrome-free composition, and Hostatint™ UV 100 is a reformulated range of pigment preparations for radiation-cured wood coatings.

Visit [Heubach](https://www.sudarshan.com/newsroom/sudarshan-chemical-completes-acquisition-of-heubach-group/) at Booth 427 in Hall 3C to learn more about these pigments.

**Vencorex Crosslinkers, Hardeners, and Isocyanate Monomers**

Vencorex, a producer of aliphatic isocyanates and their derivatives, will unveil several products at ECS: Easaqua™, Tolonate™, and HDI and IPDI isocyanate monomers.

Easaqua™ crosslinkers are designed for 2K waterborne polyurethanes as they are easy to mix in water. Vencorex says that products in this line can be used with matte and high-gloss primers and finishes, and some have fast-drying properties.

Tolonate™ are reference polyisocyanate hardeners of high-performance polyurethane coatings and adhesives. The company says that they enable good durability and extended service life. The range includes low-viscosity grades, which are essential in the development of solvent-free and high-solids formulations, and which have low- or even zero-VOC content, according to Vencorex. The line also includes some flexible and elastic products for polyurea and polyaspartic coatings.

HDI and IPDI isocyanate monomers, used for light-stable polyurethane dispersions (PUD) and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and UV-curable resins.

[Vencorex](https://www.vencorex.com/), which is headquartered in France, has three manufacturing sites in Grenoble, France; Freeport, TX; and Rayong, Thailand. Visit Booth 461 in Hall 3 to learn more.

**LB Group TiO2 Pigments**

LB Group, a Chinese chemical company, will be at ECS to introduce three products from its titanium dioxide pigment (TiO2) lines for coatings and inks: the BILLIONS™ R-996 pigment, BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment, and BILLIONS™ TR52.

The BILLIONS™ R-996 pigment is a sulfate-process titanium dioxide pigment designed for external and internal architectural coatings that can also be used for industrial and powder coatings. The BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment is a chloride-process titanium dioxide pigment that can produce a white hue with a blue undertone in external and internal architectural coatings. The BILLIONS™ TR52 pigment is a sulfate-process titanium dioxide pigment designed for printing inks.

Visit [LB Group](https://www.lomonbillions.global/) at Booth 5-465 in Hall 5.

**IFF Additives, Thickeners, and Binders**

New York-based IFF, a chemicals manufacturer, will be at ECS to talk about several of their products.

Lattice® NTC Colloidal Microcrystalline Cellulose is a functional, biodegradable fiber that is designed to improve formulation stability with low viscosity.

WALSRODER™ Nitrocellulose (NC) is IFF’s brand of printing inks, wood coatings, and varnishes. Products in the NC line are free-flowing and include an automated emptying device to enable a short emptying time (15–25 seconds per drum) and eliminate the need to manually lift a drum, according to IFF.

POLYOX™ Polyethylene Oxide is a water-soluble thickener, binder, film-forming polymer that is designed to improve adhesion.

ETHOCEL™ Ethylcellulose is a thickener and binder for solvent-based paints, wood coatings, and printing inks.

TEXTURECEL™ Carboxymethylcellulose is a thickener and binder in water-based coatings and ink formulations. The company says that the product offers thickening and rheology modification properties and is a natural alternative to synthetic polymers.

METHOCEL™ Cellulose Ethers are a key formulation component in paint removers and are soluble in water and many organic solvents.

Visit Stand 1-560 in Hall 1 to learn more about these six [IFF](https://www.iff.com/) products.

## Commercial profile

OMYA PERU S.A.C. (tax ID 20608572067, PERU) is active in foreign trade. Between 2021 and 2024 it recorded 200 operations, importing a CIF value of 7.7 million dollars (peak in 2024) and exporting a FOB value of 175.6 thousand dollars. Its imports concentrate on chemical products, plastics and rubber and minerals and fuels, sourced from China, Colombia and Netherlands; its exports on plastics and rubber, chemical products and minerals and fuels, shipped to Venezuela, Colombia and Chile. Goods move mainly through MARITIMA DEL CALLAO via marítimo.

Why does this profile matter?

As a buyer, OMYA PERU S.A.C. records 192 import operations worth 7.7 million dollars, concentrated in chemical products, plastics and rubber and minerals and fuels. Its key origins (China, Colombia and Netherlands) and purchasing recurrence make it a medium-volume account, attractive to suppliers seeking stable contracts in PERU.

As an exporter, OMYA PERU S.A.C. ships plastics and rubber, chemical products and minerals and fuels for a FOB value of 175.6 thousand dollars, with presence in markets such as Venezuela, Colombia and Chile. Its export profile positions it as a counterpart for international buyers in those destinations.

In logistics, OMYA PERU S.A.C. operates mainly via marítimo (87% of its shipments) entering mainly through MARITIMA DEL CALLAO. Its usual loading ports include BUENAVENTURA, QINGDAO and SHANGHAI. It works with customs agents such as HANSA ADUANAS SOCIEDAD ANONIMA and AGL GROUP ADUANAS S.A.C. and warehouses such as DT DINETPERU S.A.C.. Freight accounts for around 9% of the CIF value.

Financially, OMYA PERU S.A.C. accumulates a trade value of 7.8 million dollars. It pays duties of 669 dollars. With 200 operations and about 6925 tons moved, it represents a medium-value profile for commercial risk analysis and due diligence.

Industry Insight

## What Is Titanium Dioxide Used for in Soap Manufacturing?

Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) is one of the most widely used functional additives in the global soap and personal care manufacturing sector. When incorporated into soap bars, liquid soaps, or specialty cleansers, TiO₂ serves as a powerful opacifying agent and whitening pigment, giving products the clean, bright white appearance that consumers associate with purity and freshness.

In bar soap production, typically 0.1%–1.0% by weight of TiO₂ is added to the saponified mass during processing. This small but effective concentration delivers extraordinary visual impact — producing a solid, opaque, pearl-white finish that is virtually impossible to replicate with alternative ingredients. Beyond aesthetics, TiO₂ acts as a mild UV scattering agent, providing a degree of formulation stability.

🔬 Key Fact: Rutile-grade TiO₂ offers a refractive index of ~2.73 — the highest of any commercially available white pigment — delivering unmatched opacity and brightness in soap formulations.

Anatase-grade TiO₂ is also widely used in soap due to its softer, bluish-white tone and mild abrasive properties, which can gently assist with skin cleansing. Leading global soap manufacturers — from mass-market brands to artisan producers — rely on high-purity TiO₂ grades to ensure consistent batch-to-batch color performance across production lines.

Technical Deep Dive

## TiO₂ in Paper Coatings: Function, Performance & Industrial Role

The paper and paperboard industry is one of the largest consumers of titanium dioxide worldwide. TiO₂ is incorporated into paper coating slurries to dramatically improve the optical properties of the final sheet — enhancing brightness, whiteness, opacity, and printability. These improvements are critical for premium printing papers, packaging materials, specialty labels, and coated boards.

In paper coating applications, TiO₂ is dispersed into an aqueous coating slurry alongside clay, calcium carbonate, binders, and other functional additives. The coating is then applied to the base paper surface via blade, rod, or curtain coating methods. The result is a smooth, highly printable surface with excellent ink holdout and light reflection properties.

📄 Industry Data: The global paper coatings TiO₂ market is projected to reach USD 4.2 billion by 2030, driven by growing demand for premium packaging, digital printing substrates, and specialty coated papers across Asia-Pacific.

Rutile TiO₂ is preferred in paper coatings due to its superior scattering efficiency, weather resistance, and photostability compared to the anatase form. Surface-treated grades with alumina and silica coatings offer enhanced dispersibility and reduced photocatalytic activity, which helps protect binders and base paper fibers from degradation over time.

Core Benefits

## Why TiO₂ Is the #1 Choice for Paper Coating & Soap

From optical performance to formulation stability, titanium dioxide delivers properties that no alternative white pigment can match at comparable cost-efficiency.

⚡

### Maximum Opacity & Hiding Power

TiO₂'s extraordinary refractive index (2.55–2.73) delivers unmatched light-scattering efficiency. In paper coatings, this translates to excellent print opacity; in soap, it produces a brilliant opaque-white bar at minimal dosage levels.

🌟

### Superior Brightness & Whiteness

High-purity rutile TiO₂ grades achieve ISO brightness values exceeding 98%, making them indispensable for premium coated papers, high-white printing stocks, and luxury soap formulations where visual aesthetics are paramount.

🛡️

### UV Protection & Durability

Rutile TiO₂ acts as an effective UV-scattering agent in both soap and paper products, helping to protect formulations from photodegradation and maintaining product appearance through prolonged exposure to light and environmental conditions.

🔄

### Excellent Dispersibility

Surface-engineered TiO₂ grades with optimized particle size distribution and surface treatments offer superior dispersion in both aqueous paper coating slurries and saponified soap matrices, ensuring batch-to-batch color consistency.

✅

### Regulatory Compliance & Safety

Food-contact and cosmetic-grade TiO₂ products comply with FDA, EU Regulation 231/2012, and ISO standards, making them suitable for both personal care soap applications and food-adjacent paper packaging substrates.

💰

### Cost-Effective Performance

Due to its exceptional scattering efficiency, TiO₂ requires lower loading levels than competing white pigments such as calcium carbonate or talc to achieve equivalent opacity — resulting in overall cost savings in formulation and raw material consumption.

Market Outlook

## Commercial & Industrial Trends: TiO₂ in Soap & Paper Coatings

The global titanium dioxide market continues to evolve, with paper coatings and personal care emerging as two of the fastest-growing consumption segments driven by premiumization, sustainability demands, and Asia-Pacific market expansion.

📈

### Asia-Pacific Market Expansion

China, India, and Southeast Asia account for over 55% of global TiO₂ demand growth in the paper sector. Rising middle-class consumption is driving demand for premium packaging, coated printing papers, and branded personal care products — all requiring higher-quality TiO₂.

♻️

### Sustainability & Green Formulations

Eco-conscious brands are driving demand for TiO₂ grades with lower environmental footprints. Manufacturers are developing chloride-process TiO₂ with reduced waste streams, and waterborne paper coating systems with optimized TiO₂ loading to minimize total pigment use.

🖨️

### Digital Printing & Specialty Paper Demand

The explosive growth of digital and inkjet printing technologies is creating new demand for ultra-smooth, high-brightness coated paper substrates. These specialty papers require precisely engineered TiO₂ grades with controlled particle size and surface chemistry for optimal ink absorption.

🧴

### Premiumization in Personal Care Soap

As consumers increasingly demand luxury, artisan, and specialty soap products, formulators are turning to high-purity cosmetic-grade TiO₂ to deliver the brilliant white aesthetics required for premium product positioning — from hotels and spas to natural and organic soap brands.

🏭

### Functional Packaging Innovation

TiO₂-coated packaging papers are gaining ground in food and pharmaceutical packaging due to their ability to provide light barrier properties, delay product oxidation, and extend shelf life — unlocking new commercial opportunities beyond traditional printing stocks.

🔬

### Nano-TiO₂ & Advanced Surface Treatments

Next-generation surface-treated and nano-scale TiO₂ formulations are being developed to achieve equal optical performance at lower pigment loading, reduce processing costs, and enable new functional properties such as antimicrobial activity in specialty soap and medical paper applications.

Application Scenarios

## Deep-Dive: TiO₂ Applications in Paper Coating & Soap

Explore the full breadth of industrial and commercial scenarios where titanium dioxide for soap and paper coatings delivers measurable performance advantages.

📰

### LWC & MWC Printing Paper Coatings

Lightweight coated (LWC) and medium-weight coated (MWC) papers for magazine printing, catalogues, and commercial advertising rely on TiO₂ to achieve the high brightness and opacity required for vibrant full-color reproduction. TiO₂ is blended with ground calcium carbonate (GCC) and kaolin to optimize cost and performance.

📦

### Premium Packaging Board Coatings

Folding boxboard, liquid packaging board (LPB), and solid bleached sulfate (SBS) board manufacturers apply TiO₂-containing coatings to achieve the brilliant white, printable surfaces required for premium food, beverage, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical packaging applications.

🏷️

### Label Stock & Self-Adhesive Papers

White opaque label papers for product labeling, pharmaceutical packaging, and logistics applications require high TiO₂ loading to provide excellent opacity over varied background colors. Precisely dispersed TiO₂ ensures consistent whiteness and print quality across label surfaces.

🧼

### Bar Soap & Syndet Bars

Traditional saponified bar soaps and modern synthetic detergent bars (syndets) both use TiO₂ as the primary whitening and opacifying agent. Grades optimized for saponification compatibility ensure uniform dispersion throughout the soap matrix without interfering with lathering or skin-feel properties.

💧

### Liquid Soap & Body Wash Formulations

Liquid soap, body wash, and shampoo bar formulations incorporate micronized or dispersed TiO₂ to create pearlescent or opaque white visual effects. The non-ionic compatibility of properly surface-treated TiO₂ makes it suitable for a broad range of surfactant-based systems.

🌿

### Natural & Organic Artisan Soap

In the rapidly growing natural and artisan soap segment, cosmetic-grade TiO₂ — particularly ultramarine-compatible and soap-safe grades — is used to achieve the clean white color needed for high-contrast swirl patterns, layered designs, and branded aesthetic presentations sought by premium handmade soap markets.

🎨

### Decorative Paper & Wallpaper Coatings

Decorative laminate papers, wallcoverings, and surface finishing papers require high-opacity TiO₂ coatings to provide consistent whiteness and excellent hiding power over the base substrate. This ensures that the decorative print or pattern above appears vivid, true-to-color, and free of substrate bleed-through.

🏥

### Medical & Pharmaceutical Paper Applications

Medical wrapping papers, drug-release matrices, and pharmaceutical leaflet papers utilize specialty TiO₂ grades to meet strict regulatory purity standards while delivering the printability and whiteness necessary for professional medical and healthcare packaging applications.

Titanium Dioxide Lomon R-996 An Overview of Manufacturers and Applications

Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is one of the most widely used white pigments in the world, known for its exceptional brightness and opacity. Among the various grades of titanium dioxide available on the market, Lomon R-996 stands out as a premium product, primarily manufactured by Lomon Billions Group, a leading producer of titanium dioxide.

What is Lomon R-996?

Lomon R-996 is a high-quality rutile titanium dioxide pigment that exhibits excellent whiteness, high refractive index, and outstanding durability. It is specifically designed for various applications, including paints, coatings, plastics, and paper. The product is manufactured using advanced processes that ensure consistent quality and performance, making it a preferred choice for industries that demand high standards.

Applications of Lomon R-996

One of the key attributes of Lomon R-996 is its versatility across different applications. In the paint and coatings industry, it is used to enhance the aesthetic appeal and longevity of the products. Its high opacity means that only a small amount is needed to achieve the desired coverage, thus reducing the overall cost of formulations.

In the plastics industry, Lomon R-996 contributes to the UV resistance of products, making it ideal for outdoor applications. This grade of titanium dioxide helps in stabilizing colors and preventing degradation caused by sunlight exposure. Similarly, in the paper industry, its usage improves the brightness and printability of paper products.

Moreover, Lomon R-996 is suitable for other niche applications, including cosmetics and personal care products

Global Producers of Lomon R-996

Some of these companies have invested substantially in technology to improve the quality and sustainability of their titanium dioxide products.

For instance, companies like Tronox and Chemours in North America are recognized for producing high-quality TiO2 grades, albeit with slightly different properties. In Europe, companies like Venator and Huntsman also supply titanium dioxide products catering to various industrial needs.

Sustainability and Environmental Concerns

As the demand for titanium dioxide grows, manufacturers face increasing scrutiny regarding the environmental impact of their production processes. Lomon Billions Group, in particular, is committed to adopting sustainable practices in its operations. This includes reducing waste, optimizing resource utilization, and minimizing emissions from manufacturing plants.

The industry as a whole is moving towards more sustainable alternatives, like using recycled materials and exploring alternative raw materials. Furthermore, regulatory frameworks in various regions are pushing manufacturers toward more environmentally friendly production methods.

Conclusion

Lomon R-996 is a leading grade of titanium dioxide known for its excellent properties and wide-ranging applications. As industries continue to demand high-quality pigments, manufacturers are innovating and optimizing processes to meet these needs sustainably. As users of titanium dioxide seek reliable suppliers, Lomon R-996 from Lomon Billions Group remains a top choice among manufacturers worldwide, ensuring that products maintain their quality and performance in a competitive market.

In summary, the landscape of titanium dioxide production is vibrant, with Lomon R-996 exemplifying quality, versatility, and sustainability in the industry.
